Asset type: original AI creative illustration for a Weifang cultural feature article, usable as a desktop landscape banner with a mobile portrait focal crop.
Primary request: Create one imaginative folk-art tiger inspired by the expressive, toy-like spirit of Nie Jiazhuang clay sculpture and its “mud-calling tiger” in Gaomi, Weifang. Reinterpret this clay-tiger theme through an ORIGINAL color-overprinted woodblock New Year print visual language inspired by Yangjiabu, without copying any historical print, named artisan's work, actual clay sculpture, or documented craft process. This is a cross-medium visual interpretation, not a claim that the clay tiger itself is made using woodblock printing.
Subject and composition: One round, squat, spirited clay-tiger figure seen in a dynamic three-quarter view, with bold rounded eyes, prominent brows, short sturdy paws, a stylized chest blossom and original abstract tiger markings; clearly a folk toy rather than a real tiger. Keep the complete main figure very near the center, with face, chest, body and paws inside the center 35% of the landscape width and with headroom and footroom, preserving the focal subject in a centered 9:16 mobile crop and a shallower desktop banner. Create an asymmetric diagonal sweep of oversized abstract floral forms and color blocks from lower left to upper right, so the overall composition differs substantially from a quiet ink-wash image; edge details can be cropped away.
Style and material: Bold carved black linework and layered matte color blocks with subtle woodgrain, uneven ink transfer and gently imperfect registration on warm textured paper. A vivid but sophisticated folk palette of cinnabar, coral red, warm golden yellow, leaf green and deep ink; handcrafted, flat print-like visual depth, celebratory yet refined, full-bleed landscape illustration, not a webpage or poster.
Constraints: Original imagined art only; do not depict a specific person, actual object, real village, museum scene or historical event, and do not show production steps. Absolutely no Chinese or Latin lettering, calligraphy, numerals, forehead character, labels, logo, seal, signature, watermark, border, webpage interface, photography, or glossy 3D rendering.
